mcqs.question: Which of the following lists correctly represents the general reactivity series of metals as given in NCERT Class 10?

options.A: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au > Pt
options.B: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Zn > Al > Fe > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au > Pt
options.C: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Fe > Zn > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au > Pt
options.D: Pt > Au > Ag > Cu > H > Pb > Sn > Ni > Fe > Zn > Al > Mg > Ca > Na > K

mcqs.answer: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au > Pt
mcqs.explanation: Option A lists the metals in the order of decreasing reactivity as presented in the NCERT textbook: potassium, sodium, calcium, magnesium, aluminium, zinc, iron, nickel, tin, lead, hydrogen, copper, silver, gold and platinum. Options B and C have the positions of aluminium and zinc (or iron) interchanged, which is incorrect. Option D is the exact reverse of the series. Hence, A is the only correct representation.

mcqs.question: When a strip of zinc metal is placed in a solution of copper(II) sulfate, which of the following best predicts the outcome?

options.B: Zinc metal dissolves, and copper metal is deposited on the surface.
options.C: Copper metal dissolves, and zinc metal is deposited.
options.D: Both metals precipitate as insoluble compounds.

mcqs.answer: Zinc metal dissolves, and copper metal is deposited on the surface.
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is higher than copper in the reactivity series, so it can displace copper ions from copper(II) sulfate. The reaction is Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu(s). Hence zinc goes into solution as Zn²⁺ and copper is deposited as a reddish solid. Options A, C and D describe situations that contradict the reactivity series.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand reactions of metals with salt solutions
mcqs.question: Magnesium ribbon is added to a solution of iron(II) sulfate. Which reaction will occur?

options.A: Magnesium displaces iron, forming magnesium sulfate and solid iron.
options.B: No reaction occurs because magnesium is less reactive than iron.
options.C: Iron displaces magnesium, forming iron sulfate and solid magnesium.
options.D: Both metals form a precipitate of mixed sulfates.

mcqs.answer: Magnesium displaces iron, forming magnesium sulfate and solid iron.
mcqs.explanation: Magnesium lies above iron in the reactivity series, so it can displace iron from its salt: Mg + FeSO₄ → MgSO₄ + Fe(s). Therefore iron is deposited as a solid and magnesium goes into solution. Option B is wrong because magnesium is actually more reactive. Option C reverses the direction of displacement, and option D is not a description of a displacement reaction.

mcqs.question: A student places a strip of iron in a solution of copper(II) sulfate and a strip of copper in a solution of iron(II) sulfate. Which observation correctly reflects the use of the reactivity series?

options.A: Both iron and copper deposit the metal of the solution.
options.B: Iron deposits copper, while copper shows no visible change.
options.C: Copper deposits iron, while iron shows no visible change.

mcqs.answer: Iron deposits copper, while copper shows no visible change.
mcqs.explanation: Iron is higher than copper in the reactivity series, so iron can displace copper from copper(II) sulfate, producing copper metal on the iron strip. Copper is lower than iron, so it cannot displace iron from iron(II) sulfate; therefore no visible change occurs in the copper strip. Options A and C are incorrect because only the more reactive metal can cause displacement. Option D ignores the reaction that does happen with iron.

mcqs.question: True or False: In the reactivity series, gold is more reactive than zinc and can displace zinc from its compounds.

options.A: True – gold can displace zinc from its compounds.
options.B: False – gold is less reactive than zinc and cannot displace it.
options.C: Partially true – gold can displace zinc only in acidic medium.
options.D: Cannot be determined without experimental data.

mcqs.answer: False – gold is less reactive than zinc and cannot displace it.
mcqs.explanation: Gold lies at the very bottom of the reactivity series, making it the least reactive metal. Zinc is much higher, so gold cannot displace zinc from any of its salts. Therefore the statement is false. Option A contradicts the series, option C adds an unfounded condition, and option D ignores the well‑established series.

mcqs.question: A metal M₁ is placed in an aqueous solution of the salt of metal M₂. If M₁ appears above M₂ in the reactivity series, which of the following will occur?

options.A: M₁ will be displaced from its own solution.
options.B: M₂ will be displaced from its solution.
options.D: Both metals will be displaced simultaneously.

mcqs.answer: M₂ will be displaced from its solution.
mcqs.explanation: When a more reactive metal (higher in the series) is introduced into a solution containing the ions of a less reactive metal, the more reactive metal donates electrons and displaces the less reactive metal from its compound. Hence M₂ ions are reduced to solid M₂, while M₁ goes into solution as M₁²⁺. Options A, C and D do not follow the principle of the reactivity series.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand reactions of metals with salt solutions
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the reactions of zinc with copper(II) sulfate and copper with zinc sulfate?

options.A: Both reactions result in the deposition of the metal of the solution.
options.B: Only the reaction of zinc with copper(II) sulfate proceeds with metal deposition.
options.C: Only the reaction of copper with zinc sulfate proceeds with metal deposition.
options.D: Neither reaction proceeds; both are non‑displacement reactions.

mcqs.answer: Only the reaction of zinc with copper(II) sulfate proceeds with metal deposition.
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is higher than copper in the series, so Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu(s) occurs, depositing copper. Copper is lower than zinc; therefore Cu + ZnSO₄ does not cause displacement, and no metal is deposited. Hence only the first reaction proceeds. Options A and C are incorrect because the second reaction does not occur, and D is wrong because the first reaction does occur.

mcqs.question:
In a competitive exam, a question asks: Which metal will be displaced from its nitrate solution when a piece of aluminium is added?
A) Sodium
B) Potassium
C) Magnesium
D) Zinc
mcqs.explanation: The reactivity series (from most to least) is K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > ... . Aluminium is less reactive than sodium, potassium and magnesium, so it cannot displace any of them. However, aluminium is more reactive than zinc, so it can displace zinc from its nitrate solution, producing aluminium nitrate and solid zinc. Therefore, option D is correct. Options A, B and C are incorrect because those metals are higher in the series than aluminium.
